name: Vision-language connector cost (MLP projector / Perceiver resampler / Q-Former)
arithmetic_intensity: The connector is a small transformer or MLP that maps vision encoder output to LLM embedding space. For a 2-layer MLP projector (LLaVA style): input dim 1024 (ViT-L hidden), output dim 4096 (LLM hidden), 256 tokens. FLOPs = 2*1024*4096*256*2 = 4.3 GFLOPs. For a Perceiver resampler (Flamingo style): 64 learned queries, cross-attention over 256 visual tokens, 8 layers. FLOPs ~ 64*256*1024*2*8*2 = 0.5 GFLOPs. For a Q-Former (BLIP-2 style): 32 learned queries, 12 layers, cross-attention over 256 visual tokens. FLOPs ~ 32*256*768*2*12*2 = 0.3 GFLOPs. The connector is negligible compared to the vision encoder itself (<5% of total vision cost).
scales_with: number of visual tokens (linear for MLP projector, constant for resampler)
number of learned queries (linear for resampler/Q-Former)
workarounds: Use MLP projector instead of Perceiver/Q-Former - simpler, fewer FLOPs, but passes all visual tokens to LLM
Use Perceiver resampler or Q-Former to compress visual tokens to fixed small count (32-64) - adds small connector cost but dramatically reduces LLM prefill cost
Use spatial merge (2x2 pixel shuffle) before connector - 4x fewer tokens, 4x less connector compute
notes: THREE CONNECTOR ARCHITECTURES: (1) MLP projector (LLaVA): 2-layer MLP, maps each visual token independently to LLM embedding space. Passes ALL visual tokens to LLM. Cost: ~4.3 GFLOPs for ViT-L/16 at 224x224 with 7B LLM. (2) Perceiver resampler (Flamingo): learned queries with cross-attention over visual tokens. Compresses variable-length visual sequence to fixed 64 tokens. Cost: ~0.5 GFLOPs. (3) Q-Former (BLIP-2): 32 learned queries, 12 layers, cross-attention. Compresses to 32 tokens. Cost: ~0.3 GFLOPs. The connector cost is negligible compared to the vision encoder, but the choice of connector has a HUGE impact on LLM prefill cost: MLP projector passes 256 tokens (224x224) or 1024 tokens (448x448) to the LLM, while Perceiver/Q-Former pass only 32-64 tokens. This is the single most important architectural decision for multimodal serving cost. The FLOP counts are derived from standard transformer FLOP formulas; the architectures are from the original papers.
